subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source, docs, and tests make persisted session defaults intentional, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because old session state can shadow later operator policy changes.

options.title: Make operator config the upper bound
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they exceed current global or agent exec policy, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep session persistence as-is
options.body: Document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing channel lanes.

options.title: Add explicit reset first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make operator config the upper bound
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they exceed current global or agent exec policy, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for the `/exec` session override behavior and tests points to this owner path.
